A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoDA and NovelSpecies. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the relocated qualitative analysis.

before.justification: v1 reports original human evaluation in Table 1 and recognition experiments on NovelSpecies, SUN, and iNaturalist in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original human evaluation and recognition experiments in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The feature extraction, filtering, image generation, verification, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Section 3.2 clarifies how feature-conditioned synthetic images are generated for generability scoring without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same iNaturalist, SUN, and NovelSpecies coverage and retain the same qualitative examples. Applications proposed in v2's limitations section are future work, not additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain All Real, Cropping, Flipping, and ARMADA in the corresponding comparisons, alongside the same CoDA variants. Additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The NovelSpecies splits, fixed-real-data and fixed-compute designs, accuracy metric, model configurations, and Appendix A.3 experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing Figure 3 case study is refined to examine spatial feature fidelity, specifically misplaced or missing frog leg spots in ARMADA and CoDA-SD-3.5 outputs. This revises the qualitative error analysis using retained examples; the quantitative ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same three-annotator evaluation and Fleiss' kappa reporting. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical numerical results. However, v1 Appendix A.1 describes CoDA-SD-3.5 as preserving all frog features, including black spots; v2 Section 6 states that it misses black spots on the legs while Recraft reproduces all three specified features.

T1.justification: The discriminability, generability, and feature-satisfaction formulas retain their mathematical substance. Adding the generator argument g to generability makes an existing dependence explicit; no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract drops its explicit efficiency claim, and the introduction narrows improvement in 'data and compute efficiency' to 'data efficiency.' The central CoDA and NovelSpecies contributions and headline accuracy claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a specific explanation linking ARMADA's failures to incomplete WikiData features and qualifies CoDA's ability to reproduce multiple detailed attributes. New Appendix A.1 explicitly identifies the focus on fine-tuning and leaves other applications for future evaluation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a project link for code and data where v1 promised release after acceptance. Section 3.2 also clarifies generability scoring; the appendix's implementation settings and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references supporting related work, the discussion of ARMADA's image-editing backbone, and future applications, including Brooks et al. (2023), Ha et al. (2025), and Sung et al. (2022). The overall novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The qualitative discussion is rewritten and moved from Appendix A.1 into a main-text Discussions section, with a new limitations subsection in the appendix. Other edits are localized grammar, cross-reference, affiliation, and acknowledgment updates.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is condensed, relabeled, given a revised caption, and moved into the main text while retaining its example images. The other figures and the three numerical tables retain essentially the same presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 qualifies the earlier overbroad description of generated feature fidelity, narrows the efficiency claim, and explicitly documents evaluation limitations. Clearer generability instructions and code/data access information also improve transparency. These are useful but limited gains, with the method and quantitative evidence unchanged.
